## Abstract

Atmospheric CO<sub>2</sub> levels are rising rapidly, yet how plants respond at the genomic level remains poorly understood. The three-dimensional (3D) organization of chromatin in the nucleus is a key regulator of gene expression and environmental response, and changes in chromatin architecture can be transmitted across generations through epigenetic mechanisms. Here, we report that elevated CO<sub>2</sub> is associated with broad 3D chromatin reorganization in *Arabidopsis thaliana*, spanning scales from chromosome-wide compartment identity to kilobase-resolution Local Chromatin Domains (LCDs) and LCD-Associated Loops (LALs). Using chromatin conformation capture and sequencing (Hi-C) across four mutant backgrounds, we show that these changes exhibit intergenerational persistence in the self-fertilized progeny of plants grown at elevated CO<sub>2</sub>, and that this persistence is sensitive to the Pol V branch of the RNA-directed DNA Methylation (RdDM) pathway rather than to upstream small RNA biogenesis. At kilobase resolution, we annotated 2,279 LCDs whose borders are enriched for transposable element loci occupied by the chromatin-silencing members Pol V and LHP1, and near a third of LCD borders are LALs. Elevated CO<sub>2</sub> is associated with LAL attenuation and altered transcript abundance at LCD borders marked by H3K27me3, implicating coordinated RdDM and Polycomb group (PcG) activity in the chromatin response to elevated CO<sub>2</sub>. Integrated transcriptome and DNA methylation analysis across all five genetic backgrounds revealed widespread changes in gene and transposable element abundance. These findings support a model in which CO<sub>2</sub>-associated chromatin reorganization confers transcriptional plasticity through persistent chromatin states shaped by the RdDM and PcG pathways.

## Footnotes

- The authors responsible for distribution of materials integral to the findings presented in this article are Scott A. Lewis (scottlewis{at}wustl.edu), R. Keith Slotkin (kslotkin{at}danforthcenter.org), and Blake C. Meyers (bcmeyers{at}ucdavis.edu)
- This revised version addresses substantive feedback received during peer review and incorporates analyses that strengthen the manuscript's conclusions. New analyses and results: LCD borders were tested for enrichment of Pol V- and LHP1-occupied TE loci using a permutation framework (n = 1,000 shuffles), yielding 2.50-fold and 1.67-fold enrichments respectively (p \< 0.001). Co-occurrence of the two enriched border populations was assessed by Fisher's exact test (OR = 3.16, CI 2.15-4.59, p = 4.5 × 10-9), revealing convergent RdDM and PcG targeting at a shared subset of LCD borders. Chromatin loop anchors in WT Control were identified using hicDetectLoops, establishing that 32.8% of LCD borders (749/2279) coincide with loop anchor regions. Of these 70.9% overlap H3K27me3 IDR peaks within 4 Kb. A methylation-invariant fragment analysis confirmed that differential Sau3AI cut-site recovery does not drive the reported Hi-C differences (Pearson r > 0.9999, KS D = 0.175, p \< 0.001; n = 341,374 fragments). Three quantitative LAL validation analyses are provided as a new supplementary figure: per-replicate aggregate O/E scores with 95% confidence intervals, batch-level replicate effects across biological growth rounds, and per-locus contact attenuation fractions across 897 unique LAL loops (59.8% attenuated in WT High, 63.3% in WT pHigh, 47.2% in nrpe1 High). Interpretive revisions: Causal and mechanistic language has been replaced throughout with calibrated associative framing. The term "epigenetic reprogramming" has been retired and replaced with specific descriptions of what exactly changes. Transgenerational observations are described as "intergenerational persistence" rather than "heritability" to accurately reflect the single-generation scope of the data. The characterization of LCD borders as "facultative heterochromatic islands" has been removed in favor of mark-specific descriptive language. All enrichment analyses using external ChIP-seq datasets are explicitly framed as reflecting baseline chromatin state rather than CO2-dependent changes in factor occupancy. Structural additions: A Limitations section has been added. The Discussion includes a new paragraph on the mechanistic divergence between nrpd1 and nrpe1, a new paragraph proposing the chromosome 2 NuMT insertion as a candidate explanation for the pericentromeric DAG enrichment observed in pHigh, and a closing synthesis paragraph consolidating the nrpe1 convergent phenotype across three independent measurements.
